subject: MAP: Acme benchmarking plan & acceptance criteria
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Lewis <sarah.lewis@acmefin.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 20 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MAP: Acme benchmarking plan & acceptance criteria

Hi Sarah,

Thanks again for taking the call yesterday. Per our discussion, attached is the Mutual Action Plan (MAP) and the performance benchmarking plan we propose for the Acme proof-of-concept. High-level goals:

- Acceptance criteria (customer visible): P95 generation latency ≤ 350 ms for 512-token requests, TTFT (time-to-first-token) ≤ 25 ms, sustained throughput >= 180 QPS across 5-minute windows for your baseline traffic profile.
- Throughput targets (engineering): sustained tokens/sec >= 45,000 for the primary model variant, peak concurrent streams support to 120 streams during burst windows.
- Unit economics target: server-side inference cost <= $0.0009/token equivalent at the baseline request distribution (we include model/quantization tradeoffs in the plan).

MAP milestones (dates are draft, see attached PDF):
1) 2026-07-21: Sign-off on MAP & security checklist
2) 2026-07-23 to 2026-07-26: Perf runs (latency & sustained QPS) + costing runs
3) 2026-07-27: Deliverables -- results CSV + summary PDF + recommended config for Dedicated pool
4) 2026-07-29: Acceptance review & production rollout plan

Acceptance criteria are explicitly measured against the P95 and sustained QPS windows; we also include TTFT and cold-start scenarios. Attached is version 3 of the plan (redwood-map-benchmark-plan-v3.pdf) with detailed run scripts, synthetic load profiles derived from the sample logs you shared, and the eval harness we will use.

Can you confirm the MAP dates above and that procurement can accept our standard trial terms (we'll keep billing/commit details until you're ready to convert)? If you have a procurement contact to loop in, please add them (I can also send a short SOW & PO template).

Thanks,

Marcus Lin
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0162

Date: Tue, 27 Jul 2026 13:22:00 -0700
Subject: MAP Results: throughput & unit-econ summary (redwood run 20260726)

Hi Sarah / Acme team,

Attached are the results from our benchmarking runs (throughput-results-20260727.csv) and a short summary PDF included in the Drive link. High-level takeaway: we met the tightened MAP acceptance target (P95 <= 320 ms) on the quantized Dedicated configuration and exceeded the sustained throughput target at the recommended operating point. Details below.

Tested model variants and runtime config:
- redwood-std-8q8 (baseline quantized float path) on a 4x A100 pool, 32-token KV caching enabled
- redwood-8q4 (aggressive quantized) on same pool with kernel optimizations and priority routing

Key metrics (512-token distribution, 80/20 chat vs single prompt):
- redwood-std-8q8: P50 = 98 ms, P95 = 338 ms (sustained 200 QPS), TTFT = 22 ms, sustained tokens/sec = 42,600
- redwood-8q4: P50 = 115 ms, P95 = 312 ms (sustained 220 QPS), TTFT = 20 ms, sustained tokens/sec = 50,400
- Cold-start spike (600 concurrent streams for 30s): 95th percentile degraded by ~18% on P95 for std-8q8; with KV warming the 8q4 path held within +8% of baseline.

Sustained QPS windows (5-min rolling averages):
- 180 QPS: both variants stable with <3% jitter
- 220 QPS: 8q4 stable; std-8q8 showed progressive queueing beyond 4 minutes without autoscale bump
- 260 QPS: marginal for a single 4x A100 pool; we recommend either autoscale headroom or Dedicated 6x A100 for this tier.

Unit economics summary (costs are Redwood internal equivalent pricing for Dedicated pool at current spot/commit mix):
- redwood-std-8q8: estimated cost = $38.40 per 1M tokens -> $0.0000384/token
- redwood-8q4: estimated cost = $31.20 per 1M tokens -> $0.0000312/token
- At observed sustained throughput (8q4 at 50.4k tokens/sec) the per-minute inference spend ~ $1.87/min (this assumes average prompt+response = 600 tokens per request at 220 QPS).

MAP acceptance check vs Acme target:
- P95: target 320 ms (Acme tightened) -> redwood-8q4 achieved 312 ms (PASS)
- TTFT: target 25 ms -> both variants PASS
- Sustained throughput: target >= 180 QPS -> both PASS; recommended operating point for cost/perf = 220 QPS on redwood-8q4

Recommendations & next steps:
1) Accept 8q4 as the production model variant for initial rollout; schedule a canary with Dedicated 4x A100 and autoscale + 20% headroom.
2) Procurement: we can provide a 30-day evaluation PO template; we'll need confirmation of region & billing contact to provision Dedicated capacity.
3) Engineering handoff: Karthik / Olga to produce the final runbook for KV cache warmup and autoscale knobs (deliver by 2026-07-29).

Attachments: throughput-results-20260727.csv (CSV, 120 KB)
Drive summary: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1a2b3c-redwood-map-v3
HubSpot deal: https://hubspot.example.com/deal/ACME-2026-07-MAP-47

If you want, I can run an additional latency-focused pass (lower concurrency, higher per-request token lengths) to stress the P99 curve; otherwise this set validates the MAP acceptance criteria.

Thanks,

Marcus Lin
